summary: This section explains how a Producer Company that used to be an inter-State co-operative society can change back into one. It requires a special vote by members or a request from creditors, followed by approval from the Tribunal. The company must also disclose all important facts and file the final orders properly.
points: A Producer Company that was once an inter-State co-operative society can apply to the Tribunal to change back.
The application needs either a two-thirds majority vote of members present and voting, or a request from creditors holding three-fourths of the total debt value.
The Tribunal will direct a meeting of members or creditors, and if a majority representing three-fourths in value agree, it can be binding.
The Tribunal must be fully satisfied that all material facts, like financial position and audit reports, have been disclosed before giving approval.
A certified copy of the Tribunal order must be filed with the Registrar and attached to future copies of the company constitution.
The company must apply for registration under the relevant co-operative laws within six months of the Tribunal sanction and report it.
example: Aarohi Producer Company Limited started as an inter-State co-operative society years ago. Now, the members and creditors want to change it back. They hold a general meeting where at least two-thirds of the members present and voting pass a resolution to apply to the Tribunal. Alternatively, creditors representing three-fourths of the total value of creditors make a request. The Tribunal directs a meeting where three-fourths in value of the voters agree to the re-conversion. After the Tribunal checks their latest financial position and grants approval, Aarohi files the order with the Registrar and applies for registration under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act within six months.
